prompt:
---
 Roblox Game Prompt: "Basket Puzzle" - 3D Match-3 Clearance Game

 Concept

 A single-player puzzle game where the player looks down into a deep basket filled with 3D fruit and vegetable toys. The player taps objects to pull them onto a 7-slot tray at the bottom of the screen. When 3 identical items land on the tray, they match and
 disappear. Clear the entire basket to win. If the tray fills to 7 with no match, the game is over.

 ---
 Camera & Scene Setup

 - Camera angle: Fixed top-down (or slight ~15° tilt for depth perception), looking straight into the basket opening.
 - Basket: A cylindrical or rounded-rectangle container, deeper than it appears. The interior walls are visible. Think of a woven wicker laundry basket.
 - Lighting: Soft overhead light with subtle ambient occlusion inside the basket to emphasize depth and layering.

 ---
 Objects (Toys)

 - 3D low-poly or stylized models of fruits and vegetables:
 - Fruits: Apple, Banana, Orange, Grape bunch, Strawberry, Watermelon slice, Pear
 - Vegetables: Carrot, Broccoli, Corn, Tomato, Eggplant, Pumpkin, Bell Pepper
 - Each level uses a subset (e.g., 5-6 types, with 3 of each minimum - always in multiples of 3 so the level is solvable).
 - Objects have distinct color and silhouette so they're identifiable from above even when overlapping.

 ---
 Physics

 - All objects are rigid bodies with Roblox physics enabled (use BasePart with collision and gravity).
 - Objects are initially spawned/dropped into the basket and settle naturally - they stack, lean, and rest on each other.
 - When an object is tapped and removed from the basket, surrounding objects react physically - they shift, tumble, or settle into the newly available space.
 - Objects deeper in the basket may be partially or fully occluded by objects on top. The player must strategically clear top layers to access lower ones.
 - Optional: subtle basket shake/vibration when items settle after a removal.

 ---
 Selection & Tray Mechanics

 1. Tap to select: Player taps a visible object in the basket.
 2. Animation: The object lifts out of the basket (tween upward + slight scale-down) and flies to the next available slot on the tray.
 3. Tray (7 slots): A horizontal bar at the bottom of the screen.
 - Items fill left-to-right into the first open slot.
 - Grouping rule: When a new item arrives, if there are already 1 or 2 of the same type on the tray, the new item slides in next to them (items shift to make room). This ensures matching items are always adjacent.
 - Match: When 3 identical items are adjacent on the tray, they flash/animate and disappear. Remaining items shift left to close the gap.
 4. Only surface-visible objects are tappable - if an object is fully buried/occluded, it cannot be selected until objects above it are removed.

 ---
 Win & Lose Conditions

 - Win: All objects removed from the basket (basket is empty). Celebrate with confetti/particle effects.
 - Lose: The 7 tray slots are all occupied and no triplet match exists. Show a "Game Over" screen with a retry option.

 ---

The basket interior is visible with soft overhead lighting and subtle ambient occlusion to emphasize the layering and depth of the contents. Inside the basket, arrange a dense, natural pile of low-poly stylized 3D fruit and vegetable toys-such as apples, bananas, oranges, carrots, broccoli, and pumpkins-randomly stacked and leaning against each other, simulating realistic physics with collisions and gravity so they settle naturally. The objects vary in color and silhouette for clear identification from above, with some partially occluded beneath others. At the bottom foreground of the scene, place a horizontal tray with seven distinct slots aligned left to right, designed to receive selected items from the basket. The tray is clearly visible and positioned so the player can see objects flying upward from the basket to fill the tray slots. The overall composition focuses on the basket as the main volume of objects, with the tray anchoring the bottom of the view, creating a clear foreground-to-background spatial hierarchy.

prompt:
Gameplay Loop:
You are building a grid-based incremental game called "Mushroom Manager". In Mushroom Manager, players are given a 8x8 grid that they place mushrooms onto. The goal of Mushroom Manager is to gain spores, a currency generated by placed mushrooms every second. There are 5 mushroom variations: Basic Shrooms generate 1 spore per second, Fever Shrooms make adjacent mushrooms generate 2x spores (effect can stack), Radio Shrooms increase the range of mushrooms with AoE effects like fever shrooms or other radio shrooms, Shy Shrooms generate 10 spores per second but generate none if adjacent to another mushroom, and Pop Shrooms generate 1 spore per second but when popped they active the pop effect 10 times instead of once. Every second, any placed mushroom has a 10% chance to become "poppable", highlighting it in yellow. Poppable shrooms can be clicked to immediately generate it's current spore amount * 10. Each mushroom type has a base cost of 10 spores, but placing the mushroom then makes the next mushroom of the same type cost 2x as much.

UI/UX: The game supports 8 players at a time, with claimable plots. Players are assigned a plot automatically upon joining. The plots contain the 8x8 playing grid, which is a green checkerboard of 4x4x4 grass material blocks. Players will see their name and avatar on a billboard in front of their plot. The shroom inventory is accessed at the bottom of the screen, displaying all mushroom types. Players can press a mushroom to select it, and then click on a grid part to place it. Alternatively, they can drag from the button and onto the grid to place it. Mushroom buttons display their current cost. If a player right clicks a mushroom (or long presses on mobile), that mushroom is deleted and the cost for that mushroom type is cut in half.

Aesthetics:
The game uses a classic, blocky Roblox aesthetic. Basic mushrooms are blue and plain. Fever shrooms are red and themed around fire. Radio Shrooms look like a satellite dish. Shy Shrooms are normal sized when active, but tiny when inactive. Pop Shrooms look like they have additional heads coming out of the main head. When Mushrooms are active on the grid, they grow and shrink in size slightly for a bouncy effect.Shrooms display how many spores they're generating over their mesh when the mouse hovers over it or the player is nearby. Popping a shroom causes the shroom to briefly grow in size with an elastic like effect, before springing back to size. Poppable shrooms are highlighted when poppable. Throughout the game, it is a priority to include fun vfx and sfx for every interaction. Interactions with UI, shrooms, etc. must always have vfx/sfx for actions such as hover, click, etc. when relevant.

Each plot is a distinct rectangular area with a low boundary or subtle divider to separate it from neighbors. In front of each plot, place a billboard displaying the player's name and avatar, facing outward toward the camera. The grid tiles serve as the main interactive space where five distinct mushroom types can be placed: Basic blue mushrooms with simple shapes, fiery red Fever mushrooms, satellite dish-shaped Radio mushrooms, Shy mushrooms that change size based on activity, and Pop mushrooms with multiple heads protruding. Mushrooms are arranged on the grid squares and exhibit subtle bouncing animations to convey activity. Highlight poppable mushrooms with a yellow glow effect. The bottom of the screen features a horizontal inventory bar showing mushroom icons with dynamic cost labels, allowing drag-and-drop or click placement onto the grid. The overall aesthetic is blocky and classic Roblox style, with clean, colorful mushroom models and lively visual effects for interactions like hover, click, and popping. The environment is open and well-lit to emphasize the vibrant mushroom plots and player billboards, creating a clear, inviting multiplayer incremental game space.
